title: Ma'aruf the Cobbler and His Wife Fatimah (ಕನ್ನಡ)

keywords: ma'aruf the cobbler and his wife fatimah
full_text:
In Cairo lived an impoverished, gentle cobbler named Ma'aruf, who was tormented daily by his quarrelsome wife, Fatimah, who demanded dishes of honey pastries which he could not afford. Fleeing her wrath in tears, Ma'aruf took refuge in an ancient ruined mosque and prayed for peace.

A benevolent Ifrit appeared, took pity on the gentle cobbler, lifted him through the air, and set him down outside the distant, magnificent city of Ikhtiyan al-Khatan in China.

There, an old childhood friend advised Ma'aruf to present himself as a wealthy merchant whose colossal caravan had been delayed on the road.

Ma'aruf’s open-handed generosity astonished the city: whenever he borrowed gold, he immediately gave it to the beggars in the street! The King, believing he was the wealthiest merchant on earth, gave him his daughter Princess Dunya in marriage.

When Ma'aruf confessed the truth to Princess Dunya—that he was only a poor cobbler without a single dirham—the noble princess loved him even more for his honesty and pure heart, and helped him escape the wrath of the suspicious vizier.

Fleeing into the desert, Ma'aruf discovered an ancient subterranean vault containing the magical ring of the Jinni Abu al-Sa'adat!

Ma'aruf used the ring not for selfish tyranny, but to summon a colossal, real caravan of a thousand camels laden with gold, silks, and jewels to fulfill his promise to the city!

He distributed the wealth to the poor, overthrew the corrupt vizier, was crowned King, and governed in peace, proving that gentle humility is rewarded by the highest blessings.
moral: Gentle patience in poverty, generosity in abundance, and honest humility triumph over adversity. [KN]
